A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MambaPEFT with matching authors, core methods, and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A and B support reliable comparison, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original VTAB-1k and commonsense-reasoning experiments, hyperparameter ablations, and hybrid PEFT search results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds results for larger vision models, VMamba, training-data-size variation, DoRA substitution, and LoRA combinations.

M1.justification: Appendix A.8 introduces the limited DoRA_p(X) variant by replacing LoRA with DoRA at the same partial projection. The original Affix-tuning, Additional-scan, Partial-tuning objectives, and two-stage hybrid search remain unchanged; Algorithm 1 and its search settings are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same 19 VTAB image-classification tasks and eight commonsense-reasoning tasks, with unchanged pre-training dataset coverage. The additions vary sample counts, splits, and model configurations within this coverage rather than introducing new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds SPT-LoRA for ViT-S, ViT-B, and ViT-tiny, and adds Adapter+ to the ViT-B/DeiT/ImageNet-1K and ViT-tiny comparisons in Table 4. Tables 1 and 8 add combined-LoRA comparators; Table 3 adds LoRA(in_proj) at every Mamba size. Table 6 newly compares DoRA_p(X) with LoRA_p(X), substantially broadening the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix A.5 introduces training-size sweeps using exchanged official VTAB training/test roles. Other additions evaluate Vim-B and VMamba-S/B configurations. Table 1 adds a relative training-time metric and changes the stated parameter-count basis from CIFAR-100 to an average across tasks. Appendix B.1 changes the reported Pythia-1.4B full-fine-tuning learning rate from 5e-5 to 5e-6.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether training-data quantity explains the vision/language differences (A.5, Figure 7), examine model-size saturation (A.6–A.7), test DoRA substitution (A.8), and vary combined LoRA placements and ranks (B.2, Table 8). These substantially extend the retained initialization, token-placement, rank, and learning-rate ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and averages across tasks without seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises projected Prompt-tuning from 54.76 to 62.54 and unprojected Affix-tuning from 54.30 to 65.04. Table 4 changes several aggregates despite unchanged task scores, including ViT-B/ImageNet-21K LoRA from 74.5 to 72.3. Pythia full-fine-tuning rows change; the 1.4B average rises from 44.8 to 50.5 alongside its revised learning rate, so this is not a matched-setting gain. Numerous new configuration and analysis results are also reported.

T1.justification: Section 2.1, Equation 2 replaces the bilinear discretization formula with an exponential zero-order-hold formula. Appendix B.2 adds mathematical search-space size calculations for simultaneous versus staged optimization. These are localized mathematical changes; the Additional-scan derivation remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: comprehensive Mamba PEFT exploration, Mamba-specific methods, hybrid search, and greater PEFT benefits for Mamba than Transformers. The conclusion reorganizes the existing findings and adds evidence pointers without materially changing these headline claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.5 qualifies the data-size interpretation by explaining that the preferred method becomes task-dependent with more data. A.6–A.7 add a possible limited-data adaptation barrier for larger vision Mamba models and discuss performance saturation. B.2 expands the rationale for preserving pre-trained behavior during hybrid search. These are focused additions to the existing interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that evaluation uses final-epoch weights, clarifies shared-task hyperparameter selection, and separates Mamba and Pythia learning-rate configurations. It reports relative training times and refines the stated A100 search-trial duration from 20–30 minutes to around 20 minutes. Code remains promised after publication in both versions.

R1.justification: v2 adds He et al. (2023) on sensitivity-aware tuning, Lian et al. (2022) on scaling and shifting features, and Zhang et al. (2024c) on gradient-based parameter selection. Related-work discussion modestly expands, while Appendix A.8 further positions the exploration as guidance for subsequent tuning methods. The overall novelty positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section ordering remain intact. v2 expands the SSM/Vim explanation, reformats the conclusion into numbered findings with cross-references, adds Appendix A.5–A.8, and expands and rearranges the hybrid-search explanation. The language and structural revisions are localized.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the evidence displays: Table 1 gains a timing column, Tables 3 and 4 gain comparison rows and model blocks, and Figure 7 adds three data-size panels. New Tables 5, 6, and 8 display VMamba, DoRA, and combined-LoRA results. The learning-rate table is restructured and relocated; Figures 1–6 and the existing algorithm are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens this benchmarking paper by directly testing the earlier data-size hypothesis within vision, checking another Mamba architecture and larger models, and adding controls for partial and combined LoRA. It also corrects Equation 2 and several inconsistent benchmark aggregates, improving mathematical and reporting reliability. The added analyses expose practical scaling limits instead of merely reporting higher scores. Some inconsistencies remain, such as differing Vim-S full-fine-tuning averages in Tables 1 and 4, and run-to-run uncertainty is still unreported.
